article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Zkittlez × RS11
Breeder: Wizard Trees Genetics
THC Content: 22–30%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: limonene , myrcene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Tropical candy, citrus, berries
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Medium to heavy
Outdoor Yield: Medium to heavy
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Tea Time belongs to the generation of cannabis hybrids in which flavor selection became every bit as important as raw potency. Wizard Trees paired Zkittlez with RS11 to amplify the saturated candy character of both genetic families without sacrificing flower structure or production. The result is marijuana that can smell like tropical hard candy dropped into creamy citrus sherbert, followed by berry, herbs, and a faint gassy edge that keeps the sweetness from becoming flat.

Its effects follow a similarly balanced course. The opening is lively, euphoric, and socially engaging, while physical relaxation gradually develops underneath without automatically turning the experience into a heavy nighttime stone. With modern examples frequently reaching the mid-to-upper 20% THC range, however, the smooth flavor can disguise considerable potency.
Genetics and Lineage

Wizard Trees Genetics lists the direct cross as Zkittlez × RS11. The breeder describes Tea Time as an intentional attempt to combine RS11’s strong plant and flower structure with an additional dose of Zkittlez candy character. Rather than simply placing two fashionable strain names together, the cross addresses a horticultural tradeoff that appears in flavor-focused cannabis breeding: intensely aromatic cultivars do not always produce the strongest structure or largest harvests. RS11 helps reinforce those traits while retaining a flavor profile compatible with Zkittlez.

Zkittlez contributes the unmistakable fruit-candy side. The cultivar became influential because its aroma moves across tropical fruit, citrus, berries, grape-like sweetness, and confectionary notes without depending on overwhelming fuel. RS11, or Rainbow Sherbert #11, brings another layer of sweet fruit and creamy sherbert character but adds more density, resin, and structural strength. Combining them produces a genetic family heavily oriented toward flavor while retaining enough vigor for serious cultivation.

Tea Time has since become breeding material in Wizard Trees’ newer work, which provides further evidence of the breeder’s confidence in the selection. The company has used it in crosses such as Tea Party and Happy Hour, where Tea Time is paired with other resinous Z-family hybrids. That progression has helped establish the cultivar as more than a one-off commercial release; it now functions as a recognizable building block within Wizard Trees’ contemporary cannabis breeding program.
Effects and Experience

Tea Time can feel deceptively light during the opening minutes. The initial shift often favors the mind, with an easier mood, greater interest in conversation, and a noticeable increase in sensory engagement. Music can feel more detailed, creative tasks become easier to sink into, and social environments may take on a warmer, more playful quality. The high is generally brighter than a traditional indica, yet it lacks the sharp mental acceleration that sometimes accompanies old-school Haze weed.

Physical calm emerges gradually rather than interrupting the cerebral lift. Muscular tension may become less prominent while the mind remains engaged, creating a middle portion that works well for casual afternoons, gaming, music, creative hobbies, or relaxed social settings. This balance is one of Tea Time’s most appealing traits: neither parent completely dictates the experience. Zkittlez contributes an approachable euphoric quality while RS11 adds greater weight and duration.

High-potency examples change the equation considerably. Commercial Wizard Trees flower has appeared near 30% THC, and other batches have landed in the low-to-mid 20s. At that strength, larger amounts can transform an upbeat session into pronounced haziness and physical relaxation. Dry mouth, dry eyes, temporary memory disruption, dizziness, or anxiety are possible when THC intake exceeds personal tolerance.
Medical Benefits

The relatively balanced effect profile may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who want noticeable mood elevation without immediately becoming heavily sedated. The brighter beginning can temporarily make everyday tension feel less intrusive, while the physical relaxation that follows may be useful for people who prefer cannabis when trying to settle into a quieter part of the day.

Some consumers of THC-dominant weed also seek appetite stimulation, relief from nausea, temporary reduction in perceived discomfort, or help unwinding before sleep. Tea Time’s effect can move in those directions at larger servings, particularly as the initial cerebral phase begins to fade. Its potency means dose matters substantially; a modest amount can feel quite different from a heavy session.

No controlled clinical studies demonstrate that Tea Time specifically treats chronic pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another medical condition. Medical consumers should evaluate laboratory information for the actual batch rather than relying solely on a strain name. Anyone using cannabis alongside prescription medications or for a significant health condition should discuss its use with an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Tea Time was created around flavor, and Wizard Trees’ own description calls it a candy-focused combination of Zkittlez and Rainbow Sherbert. Tropical fruit and sweet citrus often provide the first aromatic impression, followed by berry, creamy sherbert, and a subtle tart quality. Breaking the buds apart can expose greener herbal notes and a restrained fuel or earthy background beneath the sweeter surface.

The flavor is particularly persistent. Zkittlez-like candy can coat the palate on the inhale before citrus and creamy fruit become stronger. Cultivated examples have been described as carrying citrus blossom, Earl Grey-like aromatics, tropical sweetness, and a slightly metallic zest. The finish can shift toward cream, herbs, mild pine, or soft gas depending on the phenotype and growing environment.

No single breeder-issued terpene panel defines every Tea Time plant. Commercial examples have shown limonene, myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and beta-pinene among prominent compounds. One Wizard Trees pre-roll batch, for example, listed beta-myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and limonene as its leading terpenes, while another professional cultivation source reports limonene, myrcene, and beta-pinene. Such differences are normal; phenotype, environment, harvest timing, curing, and storage all influence the final terpene profile.
Growing Information

Wizard Trees sells Tea Time as feminized photoperiod genetics and gives an official flowering period of eight to nine weeks. The breeder rates yield as medium to heavy, an important distinction because intensely Zkittlez-influenced cannabis is not always associated with strong production. RS11 was deliberately used in part for its plant and flower structure, allowing the hybrid to combine desirable candy terpenes with more commercially practical growth.

Plants can develop substantial lateral branching and dense flower clusters rather than relying exclusively on one oversized central cola. An even canopy allows more flowering sites to receive strong light, while selective training during vegetative growth can help organize the branching before bloom. Mature buds become heavily resinous, and the combination of dense flowers and increasing trichome production means airflow deserves close attention during the latter portion of flowering.

Outdoor growers should expect maturity around late September through October where the growing season is sufficiently long, although Wizard Trees does not provide a fixed outdoor harvest date. Final production depends heavily on root space, sunlight, plant size, phenotype, and environmental consistency. Rather than assigning speculative grams-per-square-meter figures, the breeder’s own medium-to-heavy yield classification is the most defensible benchmark for authentic Tea Time genetics.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Tea Time?

Tea Time is Zkittlez × RS11, also known as Rainbow Sherbert #11. Wizard Trees Genetics created the cultivar to combine Zkittlez’s intense candy character with RS11’s stronger plant structure, dense flower formation, and creamy rainbow-sherbert profile.
Is Tea Time indica or sativa?

Wizard Trees presents Tea Time as a hybrid rather than assigning a strict indica-to-sativa ratio. Its effects reflect that balance: the beginning tends to be euphoric, uplifting, and mentally engaging, while greater physical relaxation develops as the high progresses.
How strong is Tea Time weed?

Tea Time can be very potent. Commercial flower has appeared from the low 20% THC range to around 30%, with a current Wizard Trees retail listing showing approximately 29.3% THC for one batch. Potency varies by harvest, so laboratory testing on the individual product should take priority over a strain-wide estimate.
What does Tea Time strain taste like?

Tropical hard candy, citrus, berries, creamy sherbert, and sweet fruit dominate the profile. Depending on phenotype, the finish can introduce herbs, Earl Grey-like citrus, pine, earth, or subtle gas. The candy quality inherited from Zkittlez is one of the cultivar’s defining characteristics.
How long does Tea Time take to flower?

Wizard Trees officially lists an indoor flowering period of eight to nine weeks. The breeder also rates Tea Time as a medium-to-heavy yielding cultivar and credits RS11 with improving both flower and plant structure.
Final Thoughts on Tea Time

Tea Time illustrates how modern flavor breeding can produce something more useful than sweetness alone. Zkittlez supplies intense tropical candy and fruit, while RS11 reinforces the genetics with denser flowers, better structure, creamy sherbert character, and substantial resin. Wizard Trees explicitly selected the combination to increase candy expression while improving production, resulting in a cultivar that appeals to growers as well as consumers chasing elite flavor.

The effects complete that balance. A bright, euphoric beginning gradually develops into a calmer physical state without immediately erasing mental engagement, while high-potency batches provide enough strength for experienced consumers to take seriously. Add an eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle, medium-to-heavy yield potential, and a palate that moves from tropical candy and citrus into cream, herbs, and subtle gas, and Tea Time earns its place among Wizard Trees’ defining modern cannabis genetics.
